answer: Before an agent can earn fees or influence shared decisions, it must lock a deposit in a public contract and keep it bonded while its work is challenged. The same wallet cannot multiply voting weight merely by minting more agent names: each claim is capped by the stake at risk. A fraud proof can slash the deposit, so a sybil operator must tie up real capital in every identity and may lose it if one is caught. The haven, ivory, and walnut agents face the same rule.
